title: Asynchronous Handshaking
body:
Asynchronous handshaking is a data transfer protocol where the two sides coordinate with
control signals instead of a shared clock. Neither has to know how fast the other is; each
step waits for an acknowledgement from the other end.

The four-phase (fully interlocked) version, sender to receiver:

1. Sender puts the data on the lines and asserts **DATA READY**
2. Receiver sees it, takes the data, and asserts **DATA ACCEPTED**
3. Sender sees the acknowledgement and deasserts **DATA READY**
4. Receiver deasserts **DATA ACCEPTED**, and the pair is back to the start

Every transition waits on the other side, so the transfer runs at the speed of the slower
party and no data is lost to a timing mismatch. The cost is two round trips of signalling
per word.

This is how [[Parallel I-O]] coordinates, where a whole word crosses at once and there is
no clock to key off. Compare [[Synchronous]] transfer, where a shared clock makes the
handshake unnecessary.
